messages.author: d54aba6af40f8c5e
messages.subject: Posterior Distributions for Random Slopes
parts:
Hello,

I'm loving INLA, but have a (hopefully) simple question.

I'm looking at effects of no2 on binary outcomes by region, where the no2 effects are modified by regional income levels. 

I have data for i=1,...,N (individuals) and j=1,...,J (census tract levels) with,

Individual binary outcomes y, of length N.
Individual exposures, no2, of length N.
Individual census tract indicator data, ct, of length N.
Census tract (ct) level income data, income, of size J.

I also easily create a "full" income vector of size N as, income.full = income[ct]

The model is:

logit(y) = alpha + beta*no2
where
beta = gamma_1 + gamma_2*income + error

I'm mainly interested in posteriors for region-level beta's.  
I have fit this model in JAGS, lmer and INLA, getting nearly identical results for all three.  The INLA code is:

mod.inla <- inla(y ~ 1 + no2 + no2:income.full + f(ct,no2,model="iid"),family="binomial",data=dat.inla)
b.hat.inla <- mod.inla$summary.fixed["no2","mean"] + mod.inla$summary.fixed["no2:income.full","mean"] * income + mod.inla$summary.random$ct$mean

How can I get posterior distributions for the J beta's?  In particular I'm interested in mapping Pr(beta_j > 0) for each region j.

(Note: This is a first pass scaled down version of the model.  Of course I would like to add spatial smoothing effects on the beta's in time.)

Thanks!

John

Hi,

I thought that this would be attacked using 'measurement error models';
see f.ex http://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3065

otherwise, what you ask for is 'linear combinations'; see

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-I-have-some-linear-combinations-of-the-nodes-in-the-latent-field-that-I-want-to-compute-the-posterior-marginal-of-is-that-possible-

best
H
